correctness.rationale: With V=C^n and 1<=s<=d<n, the higher Kalman locus is the projectivization of matrices admitting an invariant s-plane in a fixed d-plane L. Choose torus weights w_i=2^i (or any integral powers of two with ordered differences distinct); 2-adic valuations show all n(n-1) offdiagonal conjugation weights are distinct. The fixed points are the projective diagonal subspace P^(n-1), Euler n, and offdiagonal matrix units E_ij. When s<d every E_ij annihilates an s-plane inside L∩ker E_ij (dimension at least d-1). At s=d the only plane is L, and precisely d(n-d) units E_ij with j<=d<i fail to preserve it. For any projective complex algebraic variety, compactly supported Euler characteristic localizes to its algebraic C*-fixed locus, and equals ordinary topological Euler characteristic. Therefore chi(K_s)=n^2 for s<d and chi(K_d)=n^2-d(n-d); subtraction yields adjacent compactly-supported layers chi_c=0 for 1<=s<=d-2 and d(n-d) for the last layer. The proof does not use smoothness, nor treat Betti numbers. Independently checked weight uniqueness and fixed-locus counts for all 2<=n<=16, d<n, 1<=s<=d; that bounded test is not the all-n proof.
residual_risks: No claim about motives, Hodge or intersection cohomology; equality of Euler numbers does not imply equal homology.
For d=1 the s<d and open-layer ranges are empty; the linear last-stratum formula still holds.

value.rationale: The higher Kalman loci are a natural nested family of determinantal/singularity varieties. A uniform Euler characteristic across all proper nonlinear filtration levels despite varying codimension and singularity, together with a single nonzero open-layer Euler jump, is a motivated topological invariant and a diagnostic constraint on later cohomology calculations. The argument is short but not a mere reformulation of the known degree formulas.
